title: Latency Lighthouse - Weekly SRE Notes (2028-05-14)
content:
Purpose
Short weekly digest focusing on latency anomalies, SLO drift, and handoff notes for the week of 2028-05-08 -> 2028-05-14. Use this as the single-threaded summary for ops standups and for informing next sprint ticket prioritization.

Highlights (TL;DR)
- One moderately-severity incident (INC-2028-042) caused increased tail latency for TextGen routes on 2028-05-11 for ~36 minutes; root cause: inter-region routing flapping during a partial router topology update.
- P99 latency for token-generation API increased from 240ms -> 510ms during the window; overall SLO (99.9% < 750ms) remained met but margin reduced.
- Quick mitigations: pinned routing policy to local-region-only, rolled back partial topology change, and deployed a patch to the routing agent to avoid aggressive flapping.
- Follow-ups: instrumentation to correlate route-change events with KV cache warmup, add circuit-breaker metrics, and harden rollback checklist.

Incidents this week
1) INC-2028-042 — TextGen tail latency spike (2028-05-11 03:44 UTC -> 04:20 UTC)
   - Symptoms: elevated p95/p99 for /v1/text/generate and increased retry rate from client SDKs. Customer-visible slow responses for ~18 minutes followed by oscillations.
   - Impact: ~2.3% of requests in the US region experienced p99 > 750ms; some dev and staging tenants reported elevated error budgets. No full region outage.
   - Detection: automated latency alert (p99 breach) triggered by observability’s SRE watch rule at 03:47 UTC. Pager routed to on-call.
   - Root cause (initial): change to router topology (rolling update of node weights) triggered a flapping path selection in the smart-router. Flapping caused repeated cold-KV-cache misses on downstream inference hosts.
   - Root cause (deeper): the router update process used a weight delta that, combined with our last-minute autoscaling events, pushed traffic through less-warm hosts; the router’s hysteresis was too low.
   - Mitigation timeline:
     * 03:48 UTC — on-call (Marco) changed routing policy to region-local and disabled cross-region spill for affected routes.
     * 03:52 UTC — rolled rollback of recent topology change (manual) and restarted router agent on 2 affected coordinators.
     * 04:05 UTC — observed p99 trending down but saw oscillations due to stale KV caches; warmed caches via targeted synthetic requests.
     * 04:20 UTC — stability restored to baseline.
   - Post-incident actions: see Action items.

SLO snapshot and trends
- Token API (prod): SLO 99.9% < 750ms; this week 99.96% overall, but during window fell to 99.65% for ~36 minutes.
- Embeddings batch API: SLO 99% < 1500ms; maintained 99.995% this week.
- Error budget usage: token-api used ~1.2% of monthly error budget this week (spike accounted for ~0.35%).
- Observations: rolling updates coincide with small, repeated SLO drifts historically — need better preflight gating and canary verification focusing on latency not just error rate.

On-call handoff notes (for next shift)
- Current risk areas: router agent rollouts and the region routing policy changes planned for 2028-05-18. Expect a canary on Tuesday; owner: Sofia.
- Active tickets to watch:
  * OBS-312 (instrumentation for route-change events) — in review (Marco).
  * SRE-4041 (routing agent hysteresis knob) — planned for next sprint (Aisha).
  * INC-2028-042 follow-up (post-incident RCA doc) — draft created, needs blameless review (Liam).
- Ongoing maintenance windows: Scheduled host kernel patching in eu-west on 2028-05-16 01:00-03:00 UTC — expect brief autoscale-induced noise.
- Slack thread summary channel: #sre-latency (pinned: incident tl;dr + watch links).

Playbook and runbook edits
- Quick edit made during incident: added a "region-local pin" checklist item to the TextGen routing playbook. Change committed to docs repo (PR: observability/pull/312).
- Required edits (postmortem): add explicit cache-warmup steps and a runbook hook to trigger synthetic warmers after any topology change.
- Long-term: create an automated gating job that runs a 5-minute synthetic workload pre- and post-routing-change to measure p95/p99 before proceeding.

Action items (owners and rough ETA)
- OBS-312: Correlate route-change events with KV cache warmup metrics. Owner: Marco Chen. ETA: 2028-05-21.
- SRE-4041: Add hysteresis config + safer default for router weight deltas. Owner: Aisha Patel. ETA: 2028-05-28.
- INC-2028-042 postmortem doc: assemble timeline, RCA, and blameless recommendations. Owner: Liam O'Connor. ETA: 2028-05-17.
- Canary project: implement 5-min synthetic latency check as preflight gating for router updates. Owner: Sofia Martinez. ETA: 2028-06-04.
- Runbook: insert explicit cache-warmup step and validate via checklist. Owner: on-call rotation (next week). ETA: 2028-05-22.

Operational notes / shorthand (softer items)
- During the incident, some engineers reported confusion about which runbook to follow (textgen vs routing). Short term: add cross-link pointers in both runbooks.
- Suggestion from on-call: have a small "warmup" agent that can be throttled to warm small cohorts of hosts post-deploy instead of blasting synthetic traffic. Low-effort proof-of-concept could be done in a day.
- Reminder: avoid changing router weights and performing host kernel updates in overlapping windows — add a scheduling guard in our maintenance calendar.

Open questions / decision points
- Do we want to maintain cross-region spill as a default, or flip to region-local by default and only allow spill for burst cases? Trade-offs: cost/resiliency vs latency predictability.
- How aggressive should router hysteresis be vs traffic rebalancing speed? Need product input for acceptable transient latency.

Meeting invites and syncs
- RCA review: 2028-05-18 16:00 UTC (30m) — invite sent to eng-sre, infra, and product reliability leads.
- Runbook workshop: 2028-05-20 15:00 UTC (1h) — hands-on update session.

Appendix / links
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2028-042
- Instrumentation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/312
- Channel logs: slack://channel/#sre-latency?msg=incident-042

Notes to reviewers
- This is intended as a light-weekly; comments requested on: the proposed hysteresis values, and appetite for changing cross-region default. If you have historical numbers about cross-region benefits (cost/latency), paste into the RCA doc.

Raw on-call snippets (copied from shift notes)
- Marco: "pinned region-local, rolled topology back, warmed KV with synthetic warmers (quick script)"
- Liam: "logging gap around router weight-change event; adding more structured event IDs"
- Sofia: "schedule guard to avoid overlapping maintenance windows — will propose calendar change"

End of notes.

(If you're reading this during your shift: please add anything you saw in the morning standup; this doc is meant to surface small context that makes handoffs smoother.)
